Natural Agent: Ginger extracts (50% v/v)Prepared honey ginger mixture (50% v/v).
Method: Agar well diffusion assay, broth assay.
Micro-Organism: S. aureus, MRSA, E. coli (sensitive and resistant strains). K. pneumoniae (resistant)
Key Findings: Honey and ginger combination induced higher mean zones of inhibition than honey or ginger alone or standard antibiotic discs (methicillin, penicillin, amoxicillin).

Natural Agent: Royal jelly (sub- MIC concentrations) (3% (v/v); 2% (v/v); 1% (v/v) added to honey).
Key Findings: For each honey type there was > 90% decrease in the MIC when 3% (v/v) royal jelly was added; a 66.6% decrease when 2% (v/v) royal jelly was added and a 50% decrease in MIC when 1% (v/v) royal jelly was added.

Natural Agent: Ethyl alcohol extract of propolis (Egyptian and Saudi Arabian) (sub MIC concentrations)
Micro-Organism: S. aureus, E. coli, C. albicans, polymicrobial cultures.
Key Findings: The MIC of honey and propolis combined was lower than honey or propolis alone.
Larger zones of inhibition were seen when honey was enriched with 1% propolis.

Natural Agent: Ethanol extracts of propolis (0.1, 0.3 or 0.5%) harvested from Spain.
Micro-Organism: Microorganisms including E. coli, S. aureus, P. aeruginosa.
Key Findings: In general, enhanced antimicrobial activity was observed when honey was supplemented with propolis. The increase varied depending on the type of honey, concentration of propolis and test micro-organism.

Type of Honey: Iranian honey from Damavand district, Iran.
Key Findings: The MIC of the combination of honey, cinnamaldehyde and carvacrol was lower than honey alone (0.49µg/mL vs 114.2 μg/mL respectively). The antibacterial activity of the triple combination was reportedly greater than imipenem.

Natural Agent: Gel composed of herbal extracts of Acacia catechu, Castanea sativa, Ephedra sinica and Momia combined with honey (25%), maple saps, Phoenix dactylifera (date), pomegranate extract and Azadirachta indica gum
Key Findings: Zone of inhibition induced by the herbal gel formulation was greater than honey alone (35.1 mm vs 13.1 mm respectively).
